newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Uttar Pradesh begins first phase of polls.
newsitem.headline: India's Uttar Pradesh begins first phase of polls.

text.p: Voting began on Monday in India's northern state of Uttar Pradesh in the first round of crucial three-phase local assembly elections, officials said.
"Polling has started on schedule in each of the 135 constituencies in 21 districts of the state and everything is peaceful," Mohinder Singh, principal home secretary, told Reuters.
Voting for the remaining seats of the 425-member assembly in India's most populous state will be held on October 3 and 7.

During the polls, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition takes on the Congress party, which supports its government in Delhi, and the opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party in a triangular contest.

In Monday's polling, 33 million eligible voters will choose from among 1,830 candidates. Voting began at 7 a.m. (0130 GMT) and tens of thousands of paramilitary troops have been deployed to curb any threat of violence.
